In [[mathematics]], a '''de Branges space''' (sometimes written '''De Branges space''') is a concept in [[functional analysis]] and is constructed from a '''de Branges function'''.

The concept is named after [[Louis de Branges]] who proved numerous results regarding these spaces, especially as [[Hilbert space]]s, and used those results to prove the [[Bieberbach conjecture]].

==De  Branges functions==
A '''Hermite-Biehler function''', also known as '''de Branges function''', is an [[entire function]] ''E'' from <math>\Complex</math> to <math>\Complex</math> that satisfies the inequality <math>|E(z)| > |E(\bar z)|</math>, for all ''z'' in the [[upper half-plane|upper half of the complex plane]] <math>\Complex^+ = \{z \in \Complex \mid \operatorname{Im}(z) > 0\}</math>.

==Definition 1==
Given a Hermite-Biehler function {{math|''E''}}, the de Branges space {{math|''B''(''E'')}} is defined as the set of all [[entire function]]s ''F'' such that
<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mikhaylov |first=Alexander |last2=Mikhaylov |first2=Victor |date=2018-04-15 |title=The boundary control method and de Branges spaces. Schrödinger equation, Dirac system and discrete Schrödinger operator |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X17310910 |journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications |volume=460 |issue=2 |pages=927–953 |doi=10.1016/j.jmaa.2017.12.013 |issn=0022-247X|arxiv=1701.08424 }}</ref>

<math>B(E) = \bigg \{ F \text{ is entire } \bigg | \frac{F}{E}, \frac{F^{\#}}{E} \in H_2(\Complex^+), \int_{\reals} \bigg | \frac{F(\lambda)}{E(\lambda)} \bigg |^2 \mathrm{d}\lambda < \infty \bigg \}</math>

where:
* <math>\Complex^+ = \{z \in \Complex \mid \operatorname{Im}(z) > 0\}</math> is the open upper half of the complex plane.
* <math>F^{\#}(z) = \overline{F(\bar z)}</math>.
* <math>H_2(\Complex^+)</math> is the usual [[Hardy space]] on the open upper half plane.

==Definition 2==
A de Branges space can also be defined as all entire functions {{math|''F''}} satisfying all of the following conditions:
* <math>\int_{\Reals} |(F/E)(\lambda)|^2 d\lambda < \infty </math>
* <math>|(F/E)(z)|,|(F^{\#}/E)(z)| \leq C_F(\operatorname{Im}(z))^{(-1/2)}, \forall z \in \Complex^+</math>

==Definition 3==
There exists also an axiomatic description, useful in operator theory.

==As Hilbert spaces==
Given a de Branges space {{math|''B''(''E'')}}. Define the scalar product:
<math display="block">[F,G]=\frac{1}{\pi} \int_{\Reals} \overline{F(\lambda)} G(\lambda) \frac{d\lambda}{|E(\lambda)|^2}.</math>

A de Branges space with such a scalar product can be proven to be a [[Hilbert space]].
